newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end soft, China plays tumble.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end soft, China plays tumble.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended on a soft note on Tuesday amid heavy profit-taking in China-related plays following their recent surge and caution ahead of U.S. economic data due later, brokers said.
The Hang Seng blue-chip index closed 9.75 points, or 0.08 percent, lower at 12,600.42. Turnover was HK$11.03 billion compared with HK$13.91 billion on Monday.

"The focus is still on the red chips but this time on the downside," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities. "The futures are at a discount to the cash market, which is making people very cautious."
May Hang Seng Index futures rose 40 points to close at 12,540. The April contract, which expired on Tuesday, closed 80 points higher at 12,630.
Among the biggest losses of the day, red chip favourite Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd tumbled HK$2.60 to HK$42.30 and China Resources Enterprise Ltd fell HK$1.20 to HK$20.65.
CITIC Pacific Ltd fell HK$1.00 to HK$40.90 and China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings Co Ltd closed HK$0.20 lower at HK$7.90.
The H-share index finished on a loss of 20.10 points, or 1.90 percent, at 1,039.93.
Analysts said investors were concerned that China may take steps to curb speculation on China-related companies.

"There is some concern over what is happening. I think what they are more concerned about is where the money is coming from," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "On Monday, 60 percent of total market volume was red chips -- it's a ridiculous level."
Analysts said investors had also shied away from blue chips ahead of the release at 1230 GMT of the U.S. employment cost index for the first quarter.
"There is some U.S. information out this week which is making people cautious," said Hutcheson.
"I think the market will take some sort of cue from Wall Street overnight after the employment cost index."
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$66.25 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd fell HK$0.50 to HK$63.50.
HSBC Holdings Plc rose HK$1.00 to HK$190.00. Its HSBC Americas Inc unit reported a 33 percent rise in first quarter net income to US$115 million from US$86 million.
Hang Seng Bank Ltd shares fell HK$0.50 to HK$84.75.
